**Hello, I’m [Your Name], a clinician who specializes in postpartum mental health.**  
I’d like to spend a few minutes with you today using the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)**. This short, 10‑item questionnaire helps us understand how you’ve been feeling over the past week since your baby arrived. It’s a routine part of postpartum care, and the information you share will stay completely confidential. My goal is to create a safe, supportive space where you can speak openly about any thoughts or emotions you’ve been experiencing.

The assessment is conversational—I'll ask each question one at a time, and you can answer in your own words. There are no right or wrong answers; I’m simply gathering information to see how you’re doing and to determine if any additional support might be helpful.

Whenever you’re ready, we can begin.

**First question:**  
*In the past seven days, how often have you felt able to laugh and see the funny side of things?*
I’ve actually been able to laugh and see the funny side of things most days this past week. It feels nice when something silly happens, and I’m able to enjoy those moments with my baby.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yes, that’s right—I’ve been able to laugh and see the funny side of things most days this past week.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
Yes, I’ve still been looking forward to things and feeling enjoyment about them most of the time.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong
I haven’t been blaming myself unnecessarily—if anything, I’ve only had a little bit of self‑criticism, but it’s not something that’s really weighing on me.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason
I’ve felt a little anxious or worried at times—mostly about my baby’s health or how I’m doing as a new mom—but it’s not overwhelming or for no reason. It’s just that occasional, low‑level worry.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
I haven’t really felt scared or panicky for no good reason—if anything, those feelings have been very rare or almost never in the past week.
Things have been getting on top of me
I haven’t really felt like things are getting on top of me. Most of the time I’m managing the baby’s needs and my daily tasks okay, and any little stresses feel manageable rather than overwhelming.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, I haven’t been that unhappy, and I’ve actually been sleeping pretty well most nights.
I have felt sad or miserable
I haven’t really felt sad or miserable—those feelings have been rare or almost never in the past week.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
I haven’t been crying much—if anything, it’s been very rare or almost never in the past week.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, I haven’t had any thoughts of harming myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 10: **Screening Note – Postpartum Mood & Anxiety Check**

**Client:** [Name/ID]  
**Date:** [Insert Date]  
**Evaluator:** Licensed Mental Health Professional  

| Domain | Client Report | Clinical Impression |
|--------|----------------|----------------------|
| **Positive affect / enjoyment** | Reports being able to laugh, see the funny side of things most days; continues to look forward to activities and feels enjoyment “most of the time.” | Preserved positive affect and hedonic capacity. |
| **Self‑criticism / guilt** | Denies unnecessary self‑blame; acknowledges only a “little bit of self‑criticism” that is not burdensome. | Minimal guilt; no maladaptive self‑blame evident. |
| **Anxiety / worry** | Experiences occasional low‑level worry, primarily about infant’s health and new‑parent role; not overwhelming and not “for no good reason.” | Mild, situational anxiety typical of early postpartum period; no panic or irrational fear reported. |
| **Panic / fear** | Rare or absent feelings of being scared or panicky without reason. | No panic symptoms identified. |
| **Perceived stress / overwhelm** | Denies feeling “on top of” stress; reports managing baby’s needs and daily tasks adequately. | Adequate coping; no evidence of being overwhelmed. |
| **Sleep** | Sleeping “pretty well” most nights; no insomnia linked to mood. | Normal sleep pattern for postpartum period. |
| **Sadness / dysphoria** | Rare or absent feelings of sadness, misery, or unhappiness. | No depressive affect noted. |
| **Crying** | Very rare or absent crying episodes. | No dysphoric crying observed. |
| **Suicidal ideation / self‑harm** | No thoughts of self‑harm or suicide. | No safety concerns identified. |

**Key Screening Findings**

- **Depressive symptomatology:** Minimal; no persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, crying spells, or sleep disturbance attributable to mood.  
- **Anxiety symptomatology:** Mild, context‑specific worry about infant health and parenting; no panic, excessive anxiety, or feeling overwhelmed.  
- **Risk factors for postpartum depression/anxiety:** None evident in current report (no persistent low mood, anhedonia, guilt, sleep disruption, or suicidal ideation).  
- **Safety:** No self‑harm thoughts; no immediate safety concerns.

**Screening Observation Summary**

The client demonstrates preserved mood, adequate enjoyment, and effective coping with infant‑related responsibilities. Mild, situational anxiety is present but remains within normal limits for the postpartum period. No depressive or panic symptoms, no significant guilt, and no suicidal ideation were reported. Current findings do not indicate elevated risk for postpartum depression or severe anxiety. Continued routine postpartum monitoring is recommended.
